The coherent evolution of LRDs' large-scale environments and halo masses toward those of normal galaxies provides a plausible explanation for their declining abundance at $z < 3$, even though the underlying small-scale physical mechanisms remain elusive.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.08319.title: Fast Astronomical Transients in Archival Photographic Plates: Using optical aberrations as a tool for discerning real images, from plate artifacts
arxiv.org/abs/2606.08319.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.08319v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The detection of fast astronomical transients in photographic plates from the Palomar sky surveys conducted in the 1950s, was subject to the criticism that such transients could be just the effect of otherwise unaccounted for plate artifacts. In this paper, we show that transient images exhibit the coma aberration pattern expected from off-axis point sources recorded through the telescope optics, a signature that plate artifacts cannot naturally reproduce. Although the data does not by themselves establish the physical origin of the light that generated the images, they lend support to hypotheses that do not rely on instrumental effects to explain transients.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.19472.title: Statistical Field Theory for Weak Gravitational Lensing
arxiv.org/abs/2606.19472.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.19472v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Standard weak-lensing calculations treat lensing as a linear remapping of the matter field along the line of sight. We instead formulate lensing as a stochastic field theory for the Sachs optical scalars, driven by random Ricci-focusing and Weyl-shearing fields. With convergence and shear expressed linearly in the Sachs-scalar fluctuations, the resulting path integral generates a diagrammatic expansion for their $n$-point correlation functions, organised into linear response, nonlinear propagation, and driving-field cumulants. The conventional calculation emerges as the lowest-order, linear-propagation limit. Beyond it, nonlinear Sachs evolution couples to driving-field non-Gaussianity, mixing the matter cumulant hierarchy into the lensing hierarchy. A selection rule governs the couplings: an $n$-point observable receives a direct contribution from the $n$-point driving-field cumulant, and its leading hierarchy-mixing correction from the $(n+1)$-point cumulant via one nonlinear Sachs interaction, with higher cumulants entering only at higher order. The two-point function, for instance, receives corrections from three-point cumulants of Ricci focusing and Weyl shearing through nonlinear Sachs evolution. Rather than a restrictive approximation scheme, the formalism is a paradigm shift: a unified framework naturally accommodating path corrections, higher-order matter statistics, stochasticity, and small-scale effects.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.11805.title: HAMCOR: A physics-driven Hamiltonian framework for inferring AGN coronal geometry from X-ray reverberation lags
arxiv.org/abs/2607.11805.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.11805v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present HAMCOR (Hamiltonian-based AGN Multi-constraint CORonal inference framework), a geometry-agnostic method for inferring the X-ray coronal structure of accreting black holes using reverberation-lag measurements. Unlike conventional template-fitting approaches, HAMCOR reframes coronal geometry inference as the ground-state selection of a physical Hamiltonian. The corona is represented as a discrete emissivity distribution over a cylindrical grid, and its geometry emerges from five competing physical constraints: magnetic coherence, lag consistency, illumination consistency, pair-production stability, and energy budget feasibility. Minimisation is performed via projected gradient descent with Armijo backtracking line search on the probability simplex. We validate HAMCOR on three synthetic geometries (lamppost, column, ring) using the same grid as the real-data fits, recovering spatial correlations rho = 0.24, 0.50, 0.12 and fractional lag errors below 24 per cent. A hyperparameter sensitivity analysis confirms robustness over more than one order of magnitude in the coupling constants. We apply HAMCOR to five sources spanning seven orders of magnitude in black hole mass: four AGN observed with XMM-Newton (Mrk 335, 1H 0707-495, IRAS 13224-3809, MCG-6-30-15) and the stellar-mass black hole binary Cyg X-1 (M_bh = 14.8 M_sun), recovering consistent extended disc-corona geometries across the full mass range. We further present a multi-epoch analysis of Mrk 335 across five XMM-Newton observations (2006-2019), revealing that the coronal centroid remains stable at (R_c, z_c) ~ (6.3, 0.5) r_g across flux states spanning a factor of ~15 in reverberation lag amplitude, arguing against a collapsing or expanding lamppost. Schwarzschild-Shapiro delay corrections amount to ~79 per cent of the flat-spacetime lag on average; the recovered spatial morphology is robust to this correction.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.14794.title: Search for double-line spectroscopic binaries in RAVE survey
arxiv.org/abs/2607.14794.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.14794v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: I present a study for double-line spectroscopic binaries content in RAVE DR6 spectra, using composite spectral model. Three complementing selections found 2813 composite spectra, belonging to 2605 unique targets. Also these results were compared with automatic classification based on t-SNE map, which shows good agreement. Additionally I identified several spectra affected by problems with wavelength calibration.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.15595.title: The FAST HI 21-cm Absorption Blind Survey. III. OH Absorption Search in the 21-cm Absorber Sample and Continued HI Absorption Search
arxiv.org/abs/2607.15595.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.15595v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present the first blind search for OH 18-cm absorption with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST), conducted alongside the HI 21-cm absorption search. Our previous FAST blind HI absorption search identified 34 systems. In this work, we extend the search using 2024 and part of the 2025 CRAFTS and FASHI data (394.4 hr and 1622.1 deg$^{2}$) together with FATHOMER observations, yielding four known and three new HI absorbers, for a total of 41 HI absorption systems. We search for OH absorption in 19 HI absorption systems whose OH redshifted frequencies fall within the FAST band. The known OH absorber towards PKS 1413+135 was re-detected, making our survey the first blind survey to detect OH absorption. No new OH absorbers were identified. We examine the relationship between $N_{\rm{OH}}$ and $N_{\rm{HI}}$, applying survival analysis to account for upper limits. The analysis does not provide statistically significant evidence for either an $N_{\rm{OH}}$-$N_{\rm{HI}}$ correlation or redshift evolution of $N_{\rm{OH}}$/$N_{\rm{HI}}$. Finally, spectral stacking sets 3$\sigma$ OH column density upper limits of 4.93, 1.64, and 1.72 $T_{\rm{ex}}$/$c_{\rm{f,OH}}\times$10$^{12}$cm$^{-2}$K$^{-1}$ for associated, intervening, and combined samples, corresponding to [\rm{OH}]/[\rm{HI}] ratios of $<$1.66$\times$10$^{-8}$, $<$1.42$\times$10$^{-8}$, and $<$0.90$\times$10$^{-8}$, assuming $T_{\rm{ex}}$=10K for OH and $T_{\rm{s}}$=100K for HI. These results place the strongest constraints to date on the OH content in radio-selected HI absorbers and establish a blind-survey benchmark for future studies of molecular gas in HI-selected systems. They also demonstrate that known HI 21-cm absorbers provide an effective parent sample for systematic OH absorption searches, paving the way for future larger surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.16018.title: Infrared spectroscopy of gas-phase hydrogenated and methylated pyrenes: from laboratory spectra to the simulated 3.4 $\mu$m emission band
arxiv.org/abs/2607.16018.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.16018v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Observations of the aromatic infrared emission band at 3.3 mic often reveal satellite emission features in the 3.4 - 3.6 mic range. While the 3.3 mic band is attributed to the CH stretching vibration of polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the satellite bands - particularly its prominent 3.4 mic component - is assigned to aliphatic CH stretching vibrations in hydrogenated and methylated PAH-like species. Our aim is to derive state-of-the-art infrared emission spectra for aliphatic-containing pyrene derivatives and compare them with astronomical observations. This will help refine our understanding of the contribution of these species to the 3.4 mic emission band. Mid-infrared spectra (1.4-25 mic of gas-phase dihydropyrene, tehtrahydropyrene, hexahydropyrene methylated pyrene, and pyrene were recorded at temperatures ranging from 373 to 673 K, depending on the species. The band profiles were analyzed using a multi-component fitting tool, and empirical anharmonicity laws were derived to quantify the evolution of the band positions and widths with temperature. The obtained spectral data was combined with the results of a Monte Carlo emission model to simulate the emission spectra following UV-photon absorption, up to the dissociation limit (<6 eV). The resulting synthetic spectra were compared with James Webb Space Telescope observations of the Orion Bar region (PDRs4All program). Based on these state-of-the-art simulated spectra, we show that 1,2,3,6,7,8-hexahydropyrene matches all the constrains to fit the red component of the 3.4 mic band observed at 3.403 mic. While 1-methylpyrene may also contribute to the underlying emission plateau, its lack of a strong infrared band complicates detection in observed spectra, unlike hexahydropyrene. All experimental spectra and their temperature-dependent analyses are available in the new cosmicPAH-IRDB database.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.01227.title: The PSR J0435+3233 Triple System
arxiv.org/abs/2608.01227.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.01227v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The detailed evolution of triple star systems is complicated and poorly known. Using archived optical/infrared and $\gamma$-ray data, we identified the pulsar PSR~J0435+3233 as a $\gamma$-ray pulsar in a hierarchical triple system, with a helium white dwarf (WD) as a close inner binary companion and a Sun-like star as the distant tertiary. PSR~J0435+3233 and the WD companion are in a circular orbit with a period of $P_{\rm orb1} = 8.0$~days and an eccentricity of $e=0.00016$. The tertiary is a G-type subgiant with a mass of $0.98(12) M_\odot$ at a distance of $2.1(4)$ kpc from the Earth. By simultaneously fitting the observed spin-period variations of the $\gamma$-ray emission (over 16.7 years) and radio emission (over 4.9 years) from PSR~J0435+3233, the changes in the inner orbital parameters, the Shapiro delay, Gaia astrometry, and the outer companion mass, we determined the outer elliptical orbit for the tertiary, with a period $P_{\rm orb2} = 73.5$~yrs and an eccentricity $e_2 = 0.598$. The outer orbit is either nearly perpendicular to the inner orbit with a mutual inclination of $\sim 85^\circ$, or moderately inclined by $\sim 54^\circ$. For the former geometry, the pulsar, the WD, and the tertiary star have masses of $1.16(5) M_\odot$, $0.273(8) M_\odot$, and $0.91(5) M_\odot$, respectively; for the latter geometry, the corresponding masses are $1.34(15) M_\odot$, $0.305(23) M_\odot$, and $1.13(7) M_\odot$. This is a unique triple system for detailed multi-band observations and for studying the evolutionary path and dynamic processes of a primordial triple star system. It will ultimately evolve into a system consisting of a neutron star and two white dwarfs.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.26731.title: Carbon in J0815+4729: Casting a shadow of doubt on the interpretation of CH absorption in the most primitive stars
arxiv.org/abs/2608.26731.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.26731v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Aims. We revisit the carbon abundance in the primitive iron-poor star J0815+4729 ([Fe/H] = -5.49). J0815+4729 is so carbon-enhanced and oxygen-rich that, in addition to CH and C2 molecular lines, weaker neutral atomic transitions are measurable in its spectrum, providing a unique opportunity to explore the line formation of C I and O I transitions in such an extremely iron-deficient star. Methods. Based on high-resolution spectroscopy and newly constructed atomic models for carbon and oxygen, we present the first investigation to derive carbon and oxygen abundances of this hyper iron-poor star from neutral atomic transitions under non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) conditions. Results. The carbon abundance derived from C I lines is A(C)NLTE = 8.08+-0.07, consistent with that inferred from C2 lines (A(C)LTE =7.96 +- 0.08), but around 0.6 dex higher than the value from CH lines (A(C)LTE = 7.47 +- 0.17). Since CH lines are the most commonly-used carbon abundance indicator for extremely metal-poor stars, this result casts doubt on the quantitative interpretation of CH absorption in the most primitive stars. We confirm that J0815+4729 is one of the most carbon-enhanced stars with [Fe/H] <= -4.5 known to date. We have also determined A(O)NLTE as 7.25 +- 0.11, with NLTE corrections of around -0.11 dex. The carbon-to-oxygen ratio of the star is [C/O] = 1.06 +- 0.1.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.08939.title: Optical Depths from the Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect with ACT DR6 and DESI DR1 Spectroscopic Galaxies and Optically-Selected Clusters
arxiv.org/abs/2609.08939.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.08939v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present stacked thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect measurements for three samples of galaxy groups and clusters: those traced by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI DR1) luminous red galaxies (LRG) and the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Sample (BGS), and an eROMaPPer optically-selected sample from the DESI Legacy Imaging Survey. We use the latest Atacama Cosmology Telescope DR6 (ACT)+Planck component-separated internal linear combination (ILC) Compton-$y$ maps and ACT+Planck coadded 90, 150, and 220 GHz temperature maps to extract the tSZ signal within a $\sim2'$ disk aperture for sources binned by luminosity, richness, or mass. We measure the average tSZ signal with high statistical significance, with signal-to-noise ratios surpassing 38 for LRG, 27 for BGS, and 39 for the eROMaPPer sample using the 90 GHz ACT DR6+Planck map. We conduct a detailed study of systematics and foregrounds such as dust and cosmic infrared background (CIB) contamination, which remain a core challenge for tSZ analysis. For the LRG and BGS samples, we find that dust and radio source emission dominate the tSZ signal at scales near and below the disk aperture radius. Large-scale ($R>4'$) contamination from the CIB is less significant. We mitigate these contaminants to isolate the tSZ signal and use a combination of simulated and real measurements to develop Compton-$y-$optical depth ($\bar y-\bar \tau$) scaling relations to infer optical depths, which are found to be in agreement with values measured using the pairwise kinematic SZ effect for the same tracer samples. The $\bar y-\bar \tau$ scaling relation for the eROMaPPer sample is the first such relationship to be derived directly from SZ measurements.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.11891.title: Reconstructing Early Primordial Black Hole Domination from Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds
arxiv.org/abs/2609.11891.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.11891v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) with masses below $\mathcal{O}(10^9)$g occupy an interesting region of parameter space that is largely inaccessible to conventional observations. Despite evaporating before Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN), these PBHs can naturally generate a period of early matter domination in the early Universe. A primordial gravitational-wave background (GWB) provides a window onto this otherwise inaccessible regime, since the modified expansion history leaves a characteristic spectral feature associated with the onset and end of PBH domination. The locations of these characteristic frequencies can be used to reconstruct the underlying PBH parameters, in particular the PBH mass. For a freely propagating GWB, the location of these frequencies additionally allow the initial PBH abundance to be determined. We derive simple numerical relations that map these characteristic frequencies directly onto the PBH mass and initial abundance. Future GW experiments span a vast frequency range, providing sensitivity to PBH masses from the BBN bound of $\mathcal{O}(10^9)\,\mathrm{g}$ down to the lower bound of $\mathcal{O}(10)\,\mathrm{g}$. We find that the nanohertz signal reported by NANOGrav, if primordial in origin, is already probing PBH masses in the range $4$--$90\,\mathrm{Mg}$. GW observations therefore offer access to a vast region of PBH parameter space that is otherwise beyond the reach of current experiments.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.30232.title: Breaking the Blend: A multi-tracer kinematic decomposition method for IFS data applied to disentangling the AGN outflow and circumnuclear ring in NGC 5728 with JWST
arxiv.org/abs/2609.30232.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.30232v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Integral field spectroscopy (IFS) of the central kiloparsecs of active galactic nuclei (AGN) reveals a mixture of spatially coincident emission from star-formation and AGN feedback exciting the interstellar medium. Disentangling these components remains a challenge, as most spectral tracers are affected by both processes, limiting robust interpretation of kinematics and energetics. We present a new framework for decomposing IFS data into distinct components on a spaxel-by-spaxel basis using a multi-tracer, stacked kinematics approach. This method combines kinematic modelling with imposed flux decomposition per spaxel, quantifying the contribution of each component across the field of view. We apply this method to JWST IFS observations of the Seyfert galaxy NGC 5728 from the Galaxy Activity, Torus, and Outflow Survey (GATOS), analysing twelve mid-infrared fine-structure lines (4.49 < $\lambda$ < 25.89 $\mu$m, 7.9 < IP < 126.2 eV). We find that the circumnuclear emission can be decomposed into two dominant components: a star-forming ring and an AGN-driven biconical outflow. Our method separates these structures and recovers their detailed spatial morphology. This framework provides a general and scalable method for physically motivated component separation in IFS data, applicable across many wavelength ranges and targets, enabling reliable interpretation of complex emission line structures (or morphologies) in active galaxies and beyond.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.39603.title: An LSST-DESC Precursor Project: Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 1 $3\times2$pt in Harmonic Space
arxiv.org/abs/2609.39603.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.39603v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present the first fully photometric joint analysis of weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering (3$\times$2pt) in harmonic space with LSST-DESC analysis pipelines applied to Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 1 (HSC Y1) data. The HSC Y1 dataset, with imaging depth and galaxy number density similar to those expected for the first year of LSST observations, is an ideal testbed for validating DESC measurement and inference tools. We measure the full set of angular power spectra - cosmic shear, galaxy clustering, and galaxy-galaxy lensing - perform null tests, and correct for the impact of observing conditions on both the galaxy density and shear fields via mode deprojection. We validate our likelihood pipeline by reproducing the official HSC Y1 cosmic shear cosmological constraints with the DESC inference code. Jointly analysing all three two-point functions, we constrain $\Lambda$CDM and $w$CDM cosmologies, reporting results for cosmic shear, the combination of galaxy clustering and galaxy-galaxy lensing (2$\times$2pt), and the full 3$\times$2pt. From the joint 3$\times$2pt $\Lambda$CDM analysis we find $\Omega_m = 0.249^{+0.061}_{-0.051}$, $\sigma_8 = 0.904^{+0.098}_{-0.091}$, and $S_8 \equiv \sigma_8\sqrt{\Omega_m/0.3} = 0.821^{+0.018}_{-0.021}$. This analysis validates the complete DESC 3x2pt infrastructure on survey data, providing the foundation for the forthcoming LSST Year 1 cosmological analysis.

arxiv.org/abs/2410.02723.title: Looking for WIMPs through the neutrino fogs
arxiv.org/abs/2410.02723.excerpt:
arXiv:2410.02723v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We revisit the expected sensitivity of large-scale xenon detectors to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). Assuming current primary noise sources can be mitigated, we find that with the present discrimination power between nuclear and electron recoils, the experimental sensitivity is limited not only by atmospheric neutrinos' nuclear recoils (''nuclear recoil neutrino fog'') but also by solar neutrinos' electron-recoil events (''electron recoil neutrino fog''). While this is known by experimentalists, it is often missed or misunderstood by theorists, and we therefore emphasize this effect. We set up a realistic detector simulation to quantify the contamination of the WIMP signal from both these neutrino backgrounds. We observe that the electron-recoil background remains significant even for signal rates exceeding those of atmospheric neutrinos, as predicted by most electroweak WIMP candidates. We update the projections for the required exposure to exclude/discover a given electroweak WIMP, streamlining the computation of their signal rates and uncertainties. We show that all of the real WIMPs with zero hypercharge can be excluded (discovered) with a 50 tonne year (300 tonne year) exposure. A similar exposure will allow to probe a large portion of the viable parameter space for complex WIMP with non-zero hypercharge.

arxiv.org/abs/2506.16530.title: Neutrino Telescope Event Classification on Quantum Computers
arxiv.org/abs/2506.16530.excerpt:
arXiv:2506.16530v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Quantum computers represent a new computational paradigm with steadily improving hardware capabilities. In this article, we present the first study exploring how current quantum computers can be used to classify different neutrino event types observed in neutrino telescopes. We investigate two quantum machine learning approaches, Neural Projected Quantum Kernels (NPQKs) and Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (QCNNs), and find that both achieve classification performance comparable to classical machine learning methods across a wide energy range. By introducing a moment-of-inertia-based encoding scheme and a novel preprocessing approach, we enable efficient and scalable learning with large neutrino astronomy datasets. Tested on both simulators and the IBM Strasbourg quantum processor, the NPQK achieves a testing accuracy near 80%, with robust results above 1 TeV and close agreement between simulation and hardware performance. A simulated QCNN achieves a ~70% accuracy over the same energy range. These results underscore the promise of quantum machine learning for neutrino astronomy, paving the way for future advances as quantum hardware matures.

arxiv.org/abs/2508.16558.title: Scalar nonstandard neutrino interactions in galactic supernovae
arxiv.org/abs/2508.16558.excerpt:
arXiv:2508.16558v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We analyze the prospects for studying scalar nonstandard interactions (SNSI) using the neutrino burst from a galactic supernova (SN). SNSI modifies the resonant flavor conversion and, correspondingly, the neutronization burst signal, and may be identifiable in future multi-tonne-scale experiments, such as Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Notably, in the normal mass ordering, SNSI can lead to an anomalous (re)appearance of the neutronization-burst $\nu_e$ peak at Earth, a feature otherwise strongly suppressed in the Standard Model. We show that, in the presence of SNSI, neutrinos propagating out of the dense SN environment acquire a density-squared-dependent contribution to their mass-squared differences, which in turn modifies the energy levels of the neutrino matter eigenstates. This density-squared effect is absent in less dense environments such as the Earth or the Sun and is precisely what enables SN neutrinos to probe SNSI parameters up to 4 orders of magnitude below the values accessible to solar or terrestrial neutrino sources.

arxiv.org/abs/2509.04384.title: Prominence: A discriminator of gravitational wave signals
arxiv.org/abs/2509.04384.excerpt:
arXiv:2509.04384v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The concept of prominence is familiar to signal engineers, topographers and mountaineers. We introduce Prominence $\cal P$ as a discriminator of gravitational wave (GW) signals. We treat black hole and neutron star binaries as astrophysical background sources, and show how $\cal P$ can be used to distinguish between GW spectra produced by first-order phase transitions, domain walls and cosmic strings, and combinations thereof. Prominence can also be used to discriminate between these and off-piste sources of GWs. The uncertainty in the measured energy density in GWs at Pulsar Timing Arrays needs to be at the sub-percent to percent level for $\cal{P}$ to achieve discrimination at 3$\sigma$. LISA and ET data are expected to have sufficiently small uncertainties that Prominence can play a central role in their analysis. We define and apply a $\chi^2$ statistic based on an inner product in signal space to show that sources indistinguishable at $2\sigma$ using the signal-to-noise ratio can be distinguished using $\mathcal{P}$ with significances above and in some cases far above $3\sigma$.

arxiv.org/abs/2601.04320.title: Metastable cosmic strings are broken at the start
arxiv.org/abs/2601.04320.excerpt:
arXiv:2601.04320v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We show that metastable cosmic strings break at early times, either via finite-temperature effects or by attaching to pre-existing monopoles during network percolation. The resulting segments can be initially super-horizon in size and thus persist for a significant amount of time. If the strings do not re-percolate, the network's eventual destruction is typically due to this early-time breaking rather than late-time quantum tunnelling. Survival of strings to epochs probed by NANOGrav requires $m_M^2/\mu\gtrsim 10^3$, where $m_M$ and $\mu$ are the monopole mass and the string tension respectively, over an order of magnitude larger than previous estimates. We also revisit quantum-tunnelling induced breaking. Results from numerical simulations suggest that this occurs mainly at rare high-tension points on the strings, yielding a rate much larger than is usually assumed. We briefly discuss the related scenario of flux tubes in a dark QCD-like hidden sector with dark-quark masses above the confinement scale.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.29000.title: Fermion scattering in a Bose-Einstein condensate
arxiv.org/abs/2603.29000.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.29000v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In a recent work, we considered the propagation of fermions in the background of a scalar Bose-Einstein (BE) condensate. Using some illustrative Yukawa-type coupling models between the fermions and the scalar fields, we determined the dispersion relations of the fermions and the scalar modes in various models. To complement that work, here we consider the corresponding fermion spinors and propagators, which are required for the calculation of rates of processes involving the fermions, as well as the thermal, and/or higher order, corrections to such rates. We obtain and present here concise formulas which are useful for those applications. As an application and for illustrative purposes we specifically calculate the rate for a generic fermion (which we denote by $\chi$) with the fermions in the BE background, using commonly used models for the fermion interactions. Due to the fact that the background fermion dispersion relations are helicity dependent, the kinematics have some unique and non-standard features. For example, at a particular value of the momentum one of the fermion modes has zero group velocity, which leads to a singularity in the scattering rate of the type of the Van Hove singularity in the density of states of some condensed matter systems. The results of the framework presented here, besides their merit in their own right, can be useful in specific contexts and applications, such as cosmic-ray electron cooling through dark matter-electron scattering, and similar ones involving neutrino and/or electron propagation in a scalar Dark Matter background.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.29873.title: The Instrumented Baffle at the Input Mode Cleaner of Advanced Virgo Plus: Four years of Successful Operation as a Monitor of Stray Light
arxiv.org/abs/2603.29873.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.29873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The suspended end mirror of the Input Mode Cleaner cavity in the Advanced Virgo Plus interferometer was equipped with an instrumented baffle in Spring 2021, serving as a demonstrator of the technology in preparation for the installation of large instrumented baffles in the main arms of the interferometer. This baffle includes tens of sensors positioned near the mirror to enable monitoring of stray light within the cavity. In this contribution, we assess the stability and performance of the instrument after four years of operation. After introducing the main characteristics of the baffle, we study the distribution of stray light and show that the instrumented baffle can be used to monitor laser stability and alignment within the cavity. Finally, we perform a noise level assessment with data from the final stages of the O4b commissioning and conclude that the baffle does not introduce any additional disturbance to the normal operation of the interferometer.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.08142.title: Real versus Complex Fermion Bare Mass and Multi-Wall String Defect Annihilation
arxiv.org/abs/2606.08142.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.08142v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Particle physics models beyond the Standard Model often contain global symmetries to address various unanswered questions. However, a common criticism of theories based on global symmetries is that such symmetries are generally expected to be explicitly violated by gravitational effects at the Planck scale. In the case of a global $U(1)$ symmetry, this explicit breaking can reduce the symmetry to a discrete subgroup of $U(1)$, leading to the formation of cosmic strings attached to multiple domain walls (DWs). These DWs are usually cosmologically problematic, since their slow scaling behavior can eventually dominate the energy density of the Universe, giving rise to the well-known cosmological DW problem, which is strongly constrained by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis. In this work, we propose a mechanism for the annihilation of these DWs. If a fermion coupled to the symmetry-breaking scalar has a small bare mass, radiative corrections generate a temperature-dependent vacuum bias that drives DW collapse. As an example, we consider a majoron model with right-handed neutrinos, where gravity-induced operators produce a string-wall network. We show that a real bare Majorana mass is sufficient to induce complete DW annihilation for even-dimensional gravity-induced operators, whereas odd-dimensional operators require a complex bare Majorana mass whose phase lifts the residual vacuum degeneracy, enabling complete annihilation.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.08767.title: Fire at the Tip of the Throat: Hagedorn Phase after brane-antibrane inflation?
arxiv.org/abs/2606.08767.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.08767v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study the post-inflationary open-string Hagedorn phase in perturbatively moduli stabilized brane-antibrane inflation. In this class of models, the volume modulus is stabilized by perturbative corrections rather than by non-perturbative effects to the superpotential, thereby avoiding the standard brane-antibrane $\eta$-problem. Since inflation ends through tachyon condensation and brane-antibrane annihilation, the endpoint is intrinsically stringy and need not be described immediately by an ordinary radiation bath. We analyze whether the energy released at annihilation can drive the visible sector into an open-string Hagedorn phase, and study the consequences for dark radiation. If the Standard Model (SM) branes lie in the same throat as where the annihilation occurs, we find that a modest fraction of the released energy deposited into surviving visible open strings is sufficient to enter the Hagedorn regime and can suppress the effective number of relativistic species $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ below current observational bounds. If the SM lies in a different throat, the result depends on inter-throat energy transfer: prompt or delayed transfer can still yield a visible Hagedorn phase. However, the mechanism is most efficient when the local string scale in the SM throat is lower than or comparable to that in the annihilation throat.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.15279.title: Particle production from bubble collisions
arxiv.org/abs/2607.15279.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.15279v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Collisions of ultra-relativistic bubbles during cosmological phase transitions can produce particles much heavier than the transition scale. Previous analyses modelled this process as the off-shell decay of the scalar background. We show that its results parametrically overestimate hard particle production and depend on the gauge choice and the coordinate choice in field space. We propose an alternative formalism, analogous to the partonic description of high-energy collisions. In the ultra-relativistic limit, the colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among the quanta constituting the Lorentz-contracted walls. We apply this approach to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particle production, and study the implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production and primordial gravitational waves.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.19298.title: Gravitational wave echoes as probes of the maximum mass of strange stars in quadratic curvature-matter coupled gravity
arxiv.org/abs/2607.19298.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.19298v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy provides a powerful avenue for probing exotic compact stars. Recent analyses of GW170817 have reported possible post-merger gravitational wave echoes with a significance of $4.2\sigma$ and a dominant frequency near $72,\text{Hz}$. Such echoes may arise from ultracompact remnants possessing photon spheres that partially trap gravitational perturbations. In general relativity, photon-sphere formation requires the stellar compactness to lie between one-third and four-ninths, a condition difficult to achieve with realistic equations of state. Here, we investigate this possibility in quadratic curvature gravity with non-minimal matter coupling, considering strange stars described by the MIT bag model equation of state. By solving the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we obtain mass-radius relations and identify configurations capable of supporting photon spheres and gravitational wave echoes. The modified Buchdahl limit permits more compact stellar solutions, while photon-sphere constraints restrict the viable parameter space. We find that increasing the bag constant reduces the maximum mass and echo time, shifting the echo frequency toward the kHz regime. The echo constraints impose more stringent maximum mass-radius limits than hydrostatic equilibrium, suggesting revised maximum mass bounds for strange stars. We further compute the critical impact parameter and eikonal quasi-normal modes, demonstrating how modified gravity parameters systematically alter the photon-sphere radius and associated observational signatures. These results establish post-merger strange stars as potential GW echo sources and highlight echoes, optical shadows, and QNMs as complementary probes of modified gravity for next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.23686.title: Color-Kinematics Duality and the Double Copy in Curved Spacetimes
arxiv.org/abs/2608.23686.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.23686v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The double copy relates gravitational data to gauge-theory data, most sharply through color-kinematics duality for flat-space scattering amplitudes. This review surveys the extent to which this idea can be formulated beyond asymptotically flat backgrounds. After recalling the flat-space ingredients needed for comparison, we describe curved-space constructions for boundary correlators and scattering observables in AdS, dS, and other non-trivial backgrounds. We then review classical and field-level maps, including Kerr--Schild, Weyl, Cotton, twistor, and convolutional double copies. A separate part is devoted to self-dual sectors. Throughout, we emphasize both the common structures that survive from flat space and the obstructions introduced by curvature.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.29377.title: Joint Model-independent Constraints on the Post-Newtonian Parameter and Cosmic Curvature from Galaxy-scale Strong Lensing, SNe Ia, BAO, and Cosmic Chronometers
arxiv.org/abs/2609.29377.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.29377v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: This investigation aims to test the validity of general relativity (GR) on kiloparsec scales via galaxy-scale strong gravitational lensing (SGL) combined with multiple cosmological probes. To circumvent the circularity problem induced by the presumption of a cosmological model based on GR, we apply the distance sum rule in the Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) metric to constrain the post-Newtonian parameter gamma PPN and spatial curvature Omega k independently of any cosmological model. The study introduces two methodological improvements: (i) parameterizing the dark-energy evolution factor with second-order Chebyshev orthogonal polynomials, which ensures uniformly high convergence across the full redshift baseline while retaining Omega k as an explicit free parameter; (ii) extending the original two-probe configuration (SGL + Type Ia supernovae) to a four-probe joint analysis that includes baryon acoustic oscillations and cosmic chronometers. Our results show that gamma PPN = 1.119 (+0.072/-0.072) and Omega k = 0.101 (+0.077/-0.076) at 68% confidence. The gamma PPN value is consistent with the GR prediction of unity at 1.7 sigma, while Omega k favors a mildly open universe, with flatness consistent at 2 sigma. Taking model-independent constraints as a benchmark, we quantify the systematic shift in gamma PPN induced by eight representative dark energy models, and find that all offsets are negligible, well below the baseline 1 sigma uncertainty, with no significant bias at current precision. These results confirm that conventional strong-lensing gravity tests introduce no measurable systematic bias, validating our model-independent framework.

Even tiny changes to these constants could make liquids too thick or too thin for essential biological processes, potentially preventing life as we know it. Surprisingly, these life-friendly conditions existed billions of years before living cells appeared. The findings raise intriguing questions about why the laws of physics seem so well suited to life.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261008.title: Just 10 minutes of daily exercise could unlock deeper sleep
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261008.excerpt: Getting better sleep might be as simple as moving a little more every day. Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin found that people who exercised more frequently experienced more deep, restorative sleep, which is essential for brain recovery, memory, and emotional well-being. Surprisingly, just 10 minutes of moderate to vigorous exercise per day was associated with measurable benefits, while even light activities like walking and standing breaks were linked to better sleep and mood.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261008.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments

Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process. The findings could help researchers identify promising strategies for preventing harmful plaque formation.

universetoday.com/articles/how-will-wate.excerpt: Growing fresh food on the Moon is going to be crucial if astronauts there are ever going to eat anything other than freeze-dried rations. Since husbanding animals on the lunar surface is…difficult (to put it mildly), most mission planners believe that plants are the solution. But we still don’t entirely understand how one of the most fundamental materials to plant growth, water, operates under partial gravity. A team of researchers, led by Karl Hasenstein of the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, and including John Kiss of the Florida Institute of Technology, and Christopher McKay of NASA’s Ames Research Center, recently published a paper in Microgravity Science and Technology that lays out the physics for how water behaves at lunar gravity.

Media in space and astrophysical systems can also develop turbulence, but the physics is different because the medium is in an ionized state (known as the plasma state) and the flow motion is strongly coupled to electromagnetic fields. Furthermore, space plasma is collisionless because the medium is so dilute that the particles do not collide with each other.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261012.excerpt: Scientists have uncovered a hidden layer of organization in the brain by creating the first detailed 3D map of its lipids, the fatty molecules essential for brain structure and communication. By analyzing millions of measurements from mouse brains, researchers identified 539 distinct chemical zones, revealing patterns and boundaries that traditional brain maps have missed. Surprisingly, even white matter, once thought to be relatively uniform, contains a complex patchwork of chemically distinct regions.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261012.excerpt: A 165-million-year-old fossil has revealed an extraordinary Jurassic predator that may help explain how mammals developed one of their most important evolutionary advantages. Although only 20 inches long, Megacauda sungei was a heavyweight among early mammal relatives, swimming through ancient waterways and hunting prey with specialized teeth. Its advanced swallowing anatomy reveals an early step toward the ability to safely nurse on milk, a key development in mammalian evolution.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261011.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261011.excerpt: Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261011.title: Scientists uncover the 2.3-billion-year-old secret that helped keep Earth habitable
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261011.excerpt: Scientists may have solved a 2.3-billion-year-old mystery about how Earth maintained enough oxygen to support life. Ancient rocks reveal that phosphorus recycling in the oceans created a self-sustaining cycle that helped keep oxygen levels high, even as the planet underwent dramatic environmental changes. The discovery challenges assumptions about Earth's early atmosphere and raises new questions about why complex life took so long to emerge.

universetoday.com/articles/tiny-gold-nan.title: Tiny Gold Nanogaps Could Crack the Chirality Puzzle
universetoday.com/articles/tiny-gold-nan.excerpt:
Looking for biosignatures across the solar system requires looking for asymmetry. Amino acids, the building blocks of proteins, are famously either “left-handed” (L) or “right-handed” (D). We know abiotic processes (i.e. those that create amino acids but don’t involve life) create a 50/50 mixture of the two types, which is called a racemic mixture. But life as we know it almost exclusively relies on left-handed amino acids to fold proteins and right-handed ones to construct nucleic acids. So if we find an imbalance in the types of amino acids we analyze from somewhere in the solar system, it's a good indication that life is behind that imbalance.

Differentiating between the two “chiralities”, as they’re called, is possible, but typically requires advanced equipment and chemical disposables that make them burdensome for spaceflight applications. But a new paper in Nature Communications from researchers led by Takahito Ohshiro and Masateru Taniguchi of Osaka University offers an alternative - a solid-state quantum tunneling sensor that can read the chirality of a single amino acid molecule using basically just some gold wire.

9.headline: PET Scan Study Links Long COVID to Damage in Dopamine Neurons
9.summary: A Canadian PET scan study of 24 long‑COVID patients found reduced dopamine‑nerve‑ending density, correlating with memory, motivation and movement deficits.
highlights: Reduced dopamine‑nerve‑ending density observed in the striatum of long‑COVID participants
Severity of memory, motivation and motor slowing symptoms tracked with dopamine loss
Findings suggest long COVID may involve a dopamine‑system disorder, opening therapeutic avenues

7.headline: Disorder Can Boost Stability in Power Grids, Brain Networks and Ecosystems
7.summary: Northwestern physicists show that moderate heterogeneity in complex networks often enhances resilience, overturning the long‑held belief that uniformity is optimal.
highlights: A new mathematical framework identifies when node or link variation stabilizes networks
Random differences sometimes outperform perfectly uniform configurations
The effect spans power grids, neuronal circuits, flocking models, architected materials and ecological webs

mercury_shrinking_faster.headline: Mercury May Have Shrunk Up to 23 km Since Forming, New Study Finds
mercury_shrinking_faster.summary: A new analysis suggests Mercury’s radius decreased by as much as 23 km—10‑30 percent more than earlier estimates—due to hidden impact‑debris effects.
highlights: Mercury’s shrinkage could be up to 23 km, roughly 30 percent greater than prior models
Researchers used MESSENGER data to map surface roughness and reveal obscuring debris
The finding implies a larger metallic core, possibly altering estimates of core composition
BepiColombo will soon test these results with higher‑resolution observations

mammoth_site_age.headline: Luminescence dating pushes South Dakota Mammoth Site age beyond 160,000 years
mammoth_site_age.summary: New luminescence dates show the Black Hills sinkhole’s mammoth remains are 160,000‑232,000 years old, far older than previous radiocarbon estimates of ~26,000 years.
highlights: Luminescence dating of surrounding sand yields ages between 160,000 and 232,000 years
Previous radiocarbon dates based on bone apatite ranged 23,000‑42,000 years and were unreliable
Researchers used feldspar OSL after quartz grains were saturated
The study appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Quaternary Research (2026)

primordial_black_hole_gw_constraints.headline: LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA Data Tighten Limits on Inflation‑Driven Primordial Black Holes
primordial_black_hole_gw_constraints.summary: Analysis of O1‑O4a runs places 95% credible upper limits on curvature‑spectrum amplitudes, constraining ultra‑slow‑roll and phase‑transition inflation scenarios.
highlights: No evidence found for ultra‑slow‑roll inflation or inflationary phase‑transition signatures
95% credible upper limits on curvature‑spectrum amplitude across ground‑based detector band
Constraints on primordial black hole abundance now surpass traditional limits

15.headline: CMS delivers most comprehensive Higgs boson test, confirming Standard Model
15.summary: A combined analysis of 138 fb⁻¹ of CMS data finds the Higgs boson’s signal strength 1.01 ± 0.05, fully consistent with Standard Model predictions.
highlights: Signal strength measured as 1.01 ± 0.05, matching the Standard Model expectation
Study combines proton‑proton collisions from 2016‑2018, totaling 138 fb⁻¹
No evidence found for invisible or off‑shell Higgs decays, tightening constraints on new‑physics models

primordial_black_holes_dark_matter_const.headline: INTEGRAL/IBIS 20‑Year Survey Sets New Limits on Asteroid‑Mass Primordial Black Hole Dark Matter
primordial_black_holes_dark_matter_const.summary: A combined spectral‑morphological analysis of 20 years of INTEGRAL/IBIS data finds no hard X‑ray signal from evaporating primordial black holes, tightening dark‑matter constraints.
highlights: First search for inverse‑Compton X‑ray emission from Hawking‑evaporating primordial black holes using INTEGRAL/IBIS
Physically motivated Galactic background model includes cosmic‑ray electrons and unresolved accreting white dwarfs
Constraints cover extended mass functions and rotating primordial black holes across the asteroid‑mass window

3.headline: Vienna Researchers Unveil First Self-Stabilizing Thorium‑229 Nuclear Clock
3.summary: A team at TU Wien built a self‑stabilizing nuclear clock using thorium‑229 nuclei, achieving a precision of one‑second error over 30 million years.
highlights: The clock uses a laser‑driven transition in thorium‑229 nuclei to lock its frequency
It operates autonomously for over 24 hours without an external atomic reference
Measured relative precision reaches 10⁻¹⁵, far surpassing typical atomic clocks

2609_12370v1.headline: Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Shows Record‑High Water D/H Ratio Linked to Low Metallicity
2609_12370v1.summary: JWST data reveal 3I/ATLAS’s water D/H ratio exceeds comet values, matching models that require sub‑solar metallicity and dense cloud conditions.
highlights: Water D/H ratio in 3I/ATLAS surpasses those measured in Solar System comets
Models reproduce the ratio at metallicities ≤0.5 Z⊙ and densities ≈10⁴ cm⁻³
H₃⁺ deuteration is enhanced in low‑metallicity environments, boosting water deuteration
Methane‑to‑water D/H ratio remains consistent with comet 67P/Churyumov‑Gerasimenko

atomic_c_o_ratio_of_kelt_9b.headline: Atomic C/O Ratio Measured on Ultra‑Hot Jupiter KELT‑9b
atomic_c_o_ratio_of_kelt_9b.summary: Using MAROON‑X spectra, researchers directly measured the atomic carbon‑to‑oxygen ratio of KELT‑9b, finding it significantly lower than solar and stellar values.
highlights: Atomic C/O ratio of KELT‑9b measured as 0.20_{-0.07}^{+0.13}
Stellar C/O ratio is 0.38±0.15, while solar value is 0.59±0.07
Atmosphere shows a thermal inversion and slight metal enrichment
Volatile‑to‑refractory ratio is 1.24× solar, indicating an ice‑to‑rock proxy consistent with the host star

jwst_hubble_27_objects_2026.headline: James Webb and Hubble Reveal 27 Tiny Trans‑Neptunian Objects Preserving Pristine Surfaces
jwst_hubble_27_objects_2026.summary: Joint observations by JWST and Hubble uncovered 27 new TNOs under 40 km, showing unexpectedly unchanged colors despite billions of years of solar‑system evolution.
highlights: 27 new TNOs discovered, all under 40 km in diameter
Smallest object measured at 10 km, still retains original surface color
Both dynamically cold and hot TNOs show identical size distributions
Infrared measurements from JWST isolated size from albedo effects
Findings published as two papers in The Astronomical Journal on Sept. 8

bbn_he_measurement.headline: Large Binocular Telescope Helium Measurement Boosts Cosmology Precision
bbn_he_measurement.summary: A new primordial helium fraction measured by the Large Binocular Telescope validates cosmological parameters independent of big‑bang nucleosynthesis assumptions.
highlights: LBT’s helium fraction measurement matches CMB‑derived constraints without assuming standard BBN
Future CMB surveys need only marginal precision gains to retain BBN‑agnostic power
The result disfavors many proposed solutions to the Hubble and BAO tensions
Neutron‑lifetime anomaly inferred from LBT aligns with bottle‑experiment values, diverging from beam results

lisa_sgwb_eccentric_bbhs.headline: LISA Could Distinguish Eccentric Stellar‑Mass Black Hole Mergers in Stochastic Background
lisa_sgwb_eccentric_bbhs.summary: A new Bayesian model shows that highly eccentric stellar‑mass black‑hole binaries produce a stochastic GW signal detectable by LISA, revealing formation histories and environmental effects.
highlights: If all binaries start with eccentricity e₀ ≳ 0.9 at fₒᵣb = 10⁻⁴ Hz, the SGWB differs clearly from a circular‑binary background.
A thermal eccentricity distribution matches circular predictions only when formation occurs at fₒᵣb = 10⁻⁵ Hz.
Dense gas environments (ρ ≳ 10⁻⁷ g cm⁻³) allow LISA to separate dynamical‑friction effects from vacuum evolution.
A LISA SGWB detection would cap the maximum eccentricity of sBBHs observable by ground‑based detectors.

arxiv_2609_12743v1.headline: Interferometry Rules Out Host Star for Saturn-Mass Free-Floating Planet
arxiv_2609_12743v1.summary: High‑resolution VLTI/GRAVITY observations found no luminous companion within 90 au, strengthening evidence that KMT‑2024‑BLG‑0792/OGLE‑2024‑BLG‑0516 is a truly free‑floating Saturn‑mass planet.
highlights: Measured planet mass: 0.73 (+0.25/‑0.15) Saturn masses.
VLTI/GRAVITY observations set 5σ host‑star mass limit of 0.5–0.6 M☉.
No host detected out to projected separation of 90 au.

definium_lsd_trial_2026.headline: Definium’s LSD Therapy Cuts Anxiety Scores in Second Late‑Stage Trial
definium_lsd_trial_2026.summary: In a 12‑week, double‑blind study, a single 100‑microgram dose of DT120 reduced Hamilton Anxiety scores by 9.8 points versus 4.7 for placebo.
highlights: DT120 produced a 9.8‑point drop on the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale
Placebo group showed a 4.7‑point reduction
The net difference was 5.1 points, matching the first late‑stage trial
Patients reported anxiety improvement as early as day two after dosing

2609_12065v1.headline: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Refines Cosmic Expansion Measurements in New Joint Analyses
2609_12065v1.summary: By jointly analyzing DESI DR2 BAO data with Planck CMB observations and marginalizing BBN uncertainties, researchers obtain tighter constraints on the Hubble constant and effective neutrino species.
highlights: BAO+BBN analysis yields h = 0.6833^{+0.0048}_{-0.0053}.
Adding CMB data tightens h to 0.6823^{+0.0027}_{-0.0026}.
Investigator choices can shift cosmological parameter estimates.

cancer_aging_acceleration.headline: Accelerated Biological Aging Linked to Rising Early‑Onset Cancer in Younger Adults
cancer_aging_acceleration.summary: A new study finds that younger generations show faster biological aging, which correlates with an 8% higher risk of early‑onset solid cancers.
highlights: Younger cohorts exhibited systemic aging up to 92% of one standard deviation higher than older cohorts
Accelerated immune system aging was tied to early‑onset lung cancer, while adipose aging linked to colorectal cancer
Participants with the highest systemic aging faced a 15% greater risk of early‑onset solid cancers

quantum_entanglement_lhc_prl.headline: Oxford Physicists Confirm Quantum Entanglement in Z‑Boson Pairs at the LHC
quantum_entanglement_lhc_prl.summary: Physicists at the University of Oxford have demonstrated that quantum entanglement persists among fleeting Z bosons produced in Higgs decays at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider.
highlights: Entanglement observed in Z‑boson pairs from Higgs boson decays
Measurements made with the ATLAS detector at 13 trillion eV collision energy
Study published in Physical Review Letters, confirming one of the highest‑energy entanglement detections

merons_wse2_scienceadvances.headline: Meron Whirlpools Unveiled in Atom‑Thin Twisted WSe₂ Semiconductor
merons_wse2_scienceadvances.summary: Researchers used high‑resolution vector PFM to directly image meron and antimeron polar nanostructures in a 0.1° twisted bilayer of WSe₂, opening pathways for low‑energy devices.
highlights: Merons and antimerons observed in a marginally twisted bilayer of WSe₂
Twist angle of only 0.1° creates a moiré super‑lattice with circulating polarization
Vector PFM distinguishes twist‑induced effects from strain contributions
Combined experiment and DFT‑based molecular dynamics confirm topological nature

rna_delivery_tags_neurons.headline: m6A Tags Direct RNA Transport to Distant Neurite Branches in Developing Neurons
rna_delivery_tags_neurons.summary: A KAIST team shows that the m6A modification, read by YTHDF2, guides specific RNAs to distal axons, essential for proper neuronal development.
highlights: Deleting Mettl14 in mouse neurons reduces m6A and impairs axon projection and neurite growth.
m6A‑SAC‑seq mapped m6A sites on transcripts linked to axon development and synapse organization.
YTHDF2 partners with FMRP and motor protein KIF5C to transport m6A‑tagged RNAs along neuronal processes.

getting_photons_into_shape_for_reliable_.headline: Engineered Waveguide Reverses Photon Shape to Boost Quantum Communication Efficiency
getting_photons_into_shape_for_reliable_.summary: Researchers at TU Wien propose a dispersion‑engineered waveguide that time‑reverses photon pulses, theoretically raising absorption rates from 54% to near‑100% for quantum networks.
highlights: Photon waveform currently matches a sawtooth shape, limiting absorption to about 54%
Time‑reversing the pulse aligns it with the receiving qubit’s optimal absorption profile
Dispersion‑engineered waveguide can achieve theoretically perfect 100% absorption
Simulations show the passive approach is technically feasible

low_energy_solar_neutrinos.headline: XENONnT Detects Solar Neutrinos at Record‑Low 17 keV Energy
low_energy_solar_neutrinos.summary: Scientists using the dark‑matter detector XENONnT have observed solar neutrinos with energies as low as 17 keV, achieving a 5 σ detection.
highlights: Neutrinos with energies down to 17 keV were identified via electron scattering in XENONnT
The observation reaches the 5 σ statistical threshold, confirming a definitive detection
Previous hints from PandaX‑4T at 2.2 σ are now superseded by XENONnT’s robust result

smbh_binary_gw.headline: 3C 66B and Mrk 501 Emerge as Prime Supermassive Black Hole Binary Targets for SKAO
smbh_binary_gw.summary: A new study shows that 3C 66B and Mrk 501 likely dominate the high‑amplitude tail of the gravitational‑wave background, making them top candidates for individual detection with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory.
highlights: 3C 66B and Mrk 501 stand out from the GW background according to NANOGrav 15‑year data
Models with strong environmental hardening predict more resolvable binaries than purely GW‑driven models
SKAO is forecast to resolve tens of individual SMBH binaries, with 3C 66B robustly detectable

2609_13821v1.headline: Flavour‑Specific Neutrino Self‑Interactions Weaken CMB Coupling Limits
2609_13821v1.summary: A new analysis shows that accounting for neutrino mixing reduces cosmological bounds on flavour‑specific neutrino self‑interactions by factors of √2 or √6.
highlights: Most flavour‑specific interaction scenarios can be modeled with a combined fluid approach
CMB limits on the effective neutrino coupling weaken by √2 when two flavours interact
Limits weaken by √6 for a single interacting flavour, except for νₑ where the fluid model is less reliable

weak_lensing_circular_velocity.headline: Pseudo‑Isothermal Profile Best Fits Weak‑Lensing Circular Velocities of Isolated Galaxies
weak_lensing_circular_velocity.summary: Using KiDS weak‑lensing data, researchers show that only the pseudo‑isothermal dark‑matter model matches circular velocity curves across four baryonic mass bins.
highlights: NFW and Burkert profiles fail to fit all mass bins
Pseudo‑isothermal profile fits all four baryonic mass bins
Analysis based on weak‑lensing measurements from the KiDS survey

gw_diffraction.headline: Extended Dark Objects Reveal Frequency‑Dependent Diffraction of Gravitational Waves
gw_diffraction.summary: Researchers show that dark solitons and dark stars imprint size‑dependent diffraction patterns on gravitational‑wave signals, detectable with current and future observatories.
highlights: Finite‑size lenses alter GW waveforms when lens radius exceeds a few × 10⁶ R₍⊙₎ (M_L/100 M₍⊙₎)^{1/2}
Current LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA data constrain dark‑object masses between 10² M₍⊙₎ and 10⁵ M₍⊙₎
Future next‑generation observatories will surpass present sensitivity, probing broader dark‑sector parameter space

2609_13527v1.headline: Iron’s Incompatibility in Post‑Perovskite Stabilizes Basal Magma Oceans on Super‑Earths
2609_13527v1.summary: First‑principles simulations show iron is strongly excluded from post‑perovskite, making residual melt buoyant and allowing stable basal magma oceans up to four Earth masses.
highlights: Iron‑Mg partition coefficient K_D drops sharply with pressure between 150 GPa and 600 GPa
Residual melt becomes iron‑rich, reversing solid‑liquid density contrast
Basal magma oceans remain gravitationally stable on super‑Earths up to 4 M⊕

2609_13610v1.headline: XMM Survey Finds 66 X‑ray Discontinuities Across 116 CHEX‑MATE Clusters
2609_13610v1.summary: A systematic XMM analysis of the CHEX‑MATE sample reveals 66 surface‑brightness edges, including 32 newly identified features, in roughly 41% of the clusters.
highlights: 66 discontinuities detected, 32 of them newly discovered
Discontinuities appear in 48 of the 116 clusters, with shocks and cold fronts distinguished
~48% of clusters with extended radio emission show X‑ray edges, while ~88% of edge‑bearing clusters host diffuse radio emission

brain_shift_50_75.headline: Midlife Brain Shift Replaces Embryonic Microglia with Inflammatory Cells Between Ages 50‑75
brain_shift_50_75.summary: A new Science study shows that from age 50 to 75 the brain’s immune cells and 3‑D genome structure undergo major remodeling, heightening neurodegeneration risk.
highlights: Sharp decline of embryonic‑origin microglia in the hippocampus between ages 50‑75
Replacement by blood‑like inflammatory microglia‑like cells
Loss of cells maintaining the blood‑brain barrier
Widespread erosion of three‑dimensional genome architecture

smbh_winds_100x.headline: XRISM Reveals Supermassive Black Hole Winds 100× More Powerful Than Expected
smbh_winds_100x.summary: Astronomers using XRISM found that the quasar H1821+643 drives winds whose energy is about one hundred times higher than prior estimates, affecting 300,000 light‑years.
highlights: Winds extend roughly 300,000 light‑years beyond the host galaxy
Turbulent energy rivals several billion supernova explosions
Study based on high‑precision iron‑ion emission lines

phase3_trutakna_igan.headline: Vera's Trutakna Cuts Kidney Death Risk in Phase 3 Trial
phase3_trutakna_igan.summary: Vera Therapeutics reports that Trutakna stabilized kidney function and lowered kidney‑related death risk over two years in a Phase 3 study of IgA nephropathy patients.
highlights: Trutakna received FDA accelerated approval in July for IgA nephropathy
The Phase 3 trial followed patients for two years
The drug reduced risk of kidney‑related death and other complications

equatorial_storms_warming.headline: Tropical Extreme Rainfall Expands and Persists More as Planet Warms
equatorial_storms_warming.summary: A 45‑year study in Singapore shows that extreme tropical storms are covering larger areas and lasting longer, while peak intensities stay roughly constant.
highlights: Extreme convective storms grew in spatial extent under warming
Storm persistence increased despite unchanged peak rainfall rates
Analysis used 122 rain gauges and weather radar at 100‑meter resolution

ngc1068_hidden_outflow.headline: JWST Uncovers Hidden Supermassive Black Hole Outflow in NGC 1068
ngc1068_hidden_outflow.summary: Infrared JWST/MIRI data reveal a dust‑shrouded gas outflow in NGC 1068 that is up to 100 times more massive than previously measured.
highlights: Mid‑infrared JWST/MIRI spectroscopy detected over 20 ionized‑gas lines and 7 warm H₂ transitions.
The hidden outflow component moves ~300 km s⁻¹ faster and carries most of the mass.
Total outflow mass reaches several million solar masses, with speeds up to 2,000 km s⁻¹.
Modeling shows outflow energetics are up to 100× larger than earlier estimates, likely aided by the radio jet.

mitotic_chromosome_assembly.headline: Pre‑existing Chromatin Domains May Build Mitotic Chromosomes, New Review Shows
mitotic_chromosome_assembly.summary: A review in Trends in Genetics proposes that interphase chromatin domains act as building blocks, reorganized by condensins and physical forces into mitotic chromosomes.
highlights: Historical scaffold model identified non‑histone proteins like condensins and topoisomerase IIα as structural cores.
Recent studies show chromatin physics—electrostatic interactions, Mg²⁺, macromolecular crowding—also shape chromosome
The review suggests interphase chromatin domains serve as pre‑existing building blocks that are cross‑linked during mitosis.

black_hole_hair_ringdown.headline: Hairy Black Holes Could Reveal Their Secrets in Merger Ringdowns
black_hole_hair_ringdown.summary: New theoretical work shows that deviations from the no‑hair theorem would imprint distinct frequencies and decay rates in the gravitational‑wave ringdowns of black‑hole mergers.
highlights: Hayward and Bardeen black‑hole models produce unique ringdown signatures
Ringdown frequency and decay rate differ from standard Kerr black holes
Current detectors lack sensitivity, but future observatories may capture these effects

alma_massive_binary_star_formation.headline: ALMA Captures Formation of Eccentric Massive Protobinary via Core‑Merger Encounter
alma_massive_binary_star_formation.summary: For the first time astronomers tracked two massive young stars orbiting each other while still forming, revealing a highly eccentric, near‑parabolic core‑merger origin.
highlights: The binary IR 07299‑1651 lies ~5,500 light‑years away and shows a 200 au separation with strongly tilted disks.
Combined ALMA, VLA, JWST and VLT data allowed 3‑D orbital reconstruction over an 8‑year baseline.
The eccentric, near‑parabolic orbit and lack of a circumbinary disk rule out simple disk‑fragmentation formation.

novel_particle_beam_muon_gravity_test.headline: Cold muonium beam from PSI may test Einstein’s equivalence principle on second‑generation particles
novel_particle_beam_muon_gravity_test.summary: Physicists at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute have created a high‑intensity, super‑cold muonium beam to measure how muons fall under Earth’s gravity.
highlights: Superfluid helium at –273 °C produces a collimated muonium beam
The beam enables a gravity‑interferometer experiment on second‑generation matter
If muonium’s fall differs, it could hint at a fifth fundamental force

heat_stable_nitrogenase.headline: Heat‑Stable Nitrogenase from Deep‑Sea Archaeon Fixes Nitrogen at 90 °C
heat_stable_nitrogenase.summary: Scientists isolated a nitrogenase from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Methanocaldococcus infernus that remains active up to 98 °C, converting N₂ into ammonia.
highlights: The enzyme stays folded until 90 °C and still functions near 98 °C.
Structural analysis revealed a hybrid metallocofactor combining molybdenum, vanadium and iron features.
Researchers captured a previously unseen “turnover” state in a molybdenum‑containing nitrogenase.
Findings suggest a common ancestral mechanism for nitrogen fixation across all nitrogenase families.

mrna_clumping_prevention.headline: Cells Evolve Codon Strategies to Keep mRNA From Clumping
mrna_clumping_prevention.summary: Researchers show that natural mRNA sequences in bacteria and humans are tuned to reduce sticky interactions, preventing harmful aggregation inside cells.
highlights: Purified E. coli mRNA aggregates in vitro, but native transcripts remain soluble in vivo
Computational redesign of codons increases aggregation propensity, confirming evolutionary pressure
Human abundant mRNAs display the same reduced‑stickiness signature as bacterial transcripts

2609_17315v1.headline: LHAASO Proton Knee Suggests Super‑Heavy Dark Matter but Photon Data Disprove It
2609_17315v1.summary: A relic particle of 5 × 10⁷ GeV could explain LHAASO’s proton hardening at 0.34 PeV and the 3.3 PeV knee, yet its accompanying photons clash with observations.
highlights: Proton spectrum from LHAASO shows a hardening at 0.34 PeV and a knee at 3.3 PeV
A superheavy dark‑matter particle of mass 5 × 10⁷ GeV decaying in the Galactic halo reproduces the proton features
All three hadronic‑interaction‑model reconstructions fit the nucleon‑channel hypothesis
Predicted gamma‑ray cascade exceeds LHAASO diffuse Galactic emission by an order of magnitude
Photon fraction from the model overshoots measured cosmic‑ray photons by two orders of magnitude

2609_16740v1.headline: Nearby Galaxies Show Dark Matter Cores Smaller Than ΛCDM Predictions
2609_16740v1.summary: A study of 136 galaxies from 10^9 to 10^{11.5} M⊙ reveals central dark matter densities far below those expected from ΛCDM simulations.
highlights: Central dark matter densities decline from ~10 kpc in 10^{10} M⊙ galaxies to >50 kpc in 10^{11.5} M⊙ systems
Hydrodynamical simulations invoking baryonic feedback often predict overly steep inner density profiles
The analysis spans radii of 20–50 kpc, providing a comprehensive benchmark across a wide stellar‑mass range

2609_17275v1.headline: Murchison Widefield Array Detects First Unbiased Low‑Frequency Fast Radio Burst
2609_17275v1.summary: A wide‑field imaging survey with the Murchison Widefield Array has captured the first non‑targeted FRB below 300 MHz, confirming a comparable event rate to higher‑frequency detections.
highlights: First FRB detection below 300 MHz from a non‑targeted survey
Imaging‑based search overcomes dispersive delay and scattering challenges
Event rate matches that observed at frequencies above 400 MHz

2609_16394v1.headline: SN 2018ibb’s Light Curve Reveals Dense Circumstellar Matter Around Pair‑Instability Supernova
2609_16394v1.summary: Analysis of SN 2018ibb’s post‑peak light curve shows that interaction with dense circumstellar matter can explain its unexpected blue excess and luminosity break.
highlights: Bolometric luminosity from 150 d after peak matches models with CSM mass‑loss rate 0.01 (v_CSM/1,000 km s⁻¹) M⊙ yr⁻¹
The luminosity break at ~300 d indicates CSM interaction ended, implying a CSM radius of 8.5e16 cm
Progenitor mass loss was enhanced for ~28 (v_CSM/1,000 km s⁻¹)⁻¹ yr before explosion

hotjupiter_ngts10_phasecurve.headline: JWST Reveals Cloud Gaps and Deep Heat Transport on Hot‑Jupiter NGTS‑10 Ab
hotjupiter_ngts10_phasecurve.summary: Using JWST NIRSpec PRISM phase‑curve data, researchers mapped NGTS‑10 Ab’s reflected light and thermal emission, finding anti‑correlated clouds and temperature.
highlights: Thermal emission peaks eastward while reflected light peaks westward, showing distinct atmospheric dynamics
Clouds of micron‑sized silicate particles evaporate over the hottest eastern substellar region
Heat transport efficiency increases with depth, with a measured offset slope of 7.1 ± 1.9 ° per pressure dex

2609_16425v1.headline: Reanalysis Shows 43 GeV Gamma‑Ray Line in Galaxy Clusters Unlikely to Signal Dark Matter
2609_16425v1.summary: A fresh study of Fermi‑LAT data finds the reported 43 GeV line across Virgo, Fornax and Ophiuchus clusters has a broad spatial profile inconsistent with dark‑matter annihilation.
highlights: The excess persists in multiple event‑type partitions and independent data subsets
Uniform surface brightness across the virial region fits the signal better than a central NFW profile
Statistical significance peaks at 2.7 σ after accounting for five morphological models

brown_dwarf_weather.headline: JWST Uncovers Jupiter‑Like Weather Patterns on Brown Dwarf SIMP 0136
brown_dwarf_weather.summary: Using JWST data and principal component analysis, researchers found that SIMP 0136’s atmospheric changes are driven by just two dominant processes.
highlights: Two principal components explain most of the brown dwarf’s brightness variations
The components correspond to temperature shifts and vertical cloud structure changes
Three recurring weather states rotate into view, creating hotter, thinner‑cloud regions and cooler, thicker‑cloud zones

neutron_star_eos.headline: Universal Functional Form Accurately Captures Neutron-Star Equation‑of‑State Across Diverse Models
neutron_star_eos.summary: A new piecewise‑continuous parametrization reproduces tabulated dense‑matter equations of state and matches multimessenger neutron‑star observations with high fidelity.
highlights: Validated against tabulated EoSs from CompOSE and LALSimulation repositories
Bayesian inference using synthetic noise and multimessenger mass‑tidal data constrains parameter correlations
Fits span from very soft to very stiff EoSs, preserving macroscopic neutron‑star observables

2609_16547v1.headline: DESI Spectra Reveal No Optical Absorption from Multi‑State Dark Matter
2609_16547v1.summary: A stacking analysis of 145,087 DESI early‑release spectra finds no optical‑depth signal, setting new limits on magnetic dipole transitions of MeV‑scale dark matter.
highlights: Stacked 145,087 DESI spectra paired with foreground GAMA galaxy groups
Placed 2σ upper limits on magnetic dipole transition cross‑section for ΔE≈3–5 eV
Limits target a few MeV dark matter mass inaccessible to BBN, CMB and direct searches

gw_bias_illustristng300.headline: Machine‑Learned Merger Rates Reveal Stronger Gravitational‑Wave Bias in IllustrisTNG300
gw_bias_illustristng300.summary: A new simulation framework using a machine‑learning emulator calibrated with GALAXYRATE shows BBH mergers preferentially reside in massive, metal‑rich halos, increasing GW bias.
highlights: GW sources exhibit higher bias than the overall galaxy population
The machine‑learned model adds scale‑dependent bias beyond stellar‑mass weighting
Metallicity correlates positively with both GW and galaxy bias

cosmic_noon_miri_wfss.headline: MIRI WFSS Survey of Hubble Ultra Deep Field Reveals 3.3 µm PAH Traces Star Formation at Cosmic Noon
cosmic_noon_miri_wfss.summary: Using JWST's MIRI wide‑field slitless spectroscopy, researchers obtained spectra of 47 galaxies up to redshift 3.712, confirming the 3.3 µm PAH feature as a reliable star‑formation indicator during the Cosmic Noon era.
highlights: Spectra of 47 galaxies with confirmed redshifts were captured using MIRI WFSS in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
The 3.3 µm PAH luminosities correlate tightly with total infrared luminosity and SED‑derived star‑formation rates
Observations cover redshifts 0.67–3.1, fully spanning the peak star‑formation period known as Cosmic Noon

alzheimer_immune_cells.headline: Lymph‑Node Dendritic Cells Trigger Alzheimer’s Damage, Study Finds
alzheimer_immune_cells.summary: Researchers found that suppressing dendritic cells in lymph nodes protects mice from tau‑driven neurodegeneration, suggesting a new peripheral target for Alzheimer’s therapy.
highlights: In mice lacking lymph‑node dendritic cells, brain tau accumulation persisted but neurodegeneration was markedly reduced
Fewer T cells entered the brains of dendritic‑cell‑deficient mice, linking peripheral immune priming to brain inflammation
The study, published in Nature Neuroscience on September 3, used engineered tau‑linked mouse models to test the hypothesis

jwst_gas_outflows_dead_galaxies.headline: Webb Telescope Finds Record‑Breaking Gas Outflows in Distant Dead Galaxies
jwst_gas_outflows_dead_galaxies.summary: Astronomers using JWST/NIRSpec measured the strongest neutral‑gas outflows ever seen from quiescent galaxies 11‑13 billion years ago, yet most of the gas likely falls back.
highlights: Outflows detected in 13 of 23 massive quiescent galaxies at redshift 2.82–4.62
Neutral Na I D absorption reveals outflow rates 10–100 × higher than ionized gas
The most extreme case, galaxy DD‑236, shows a record‑high outflow linked to an active black hole

human_brain_organoid_mice_shrink.headline: Scientists Replace Missing Mouse Brain Tissue with Human Organoids in Groundbreaking Study
human_brain_organoid_mice_shrink.summary: Researchers transplanted human brain organoids into genetically modified mice lacking most of their cortex, achieving 90% integration and functional growth.
highlights: Genetically modified mice develop only 2% of their cerebral cortex and lack much of the hippocampus
Human cortical organoids were injected into the vacant space, integrating successfully in about 90% of cases
Transplanted mice displayed subtle deficits in fine‑motor skills, working memory, and socialization
The study, published in Nature, offers a new platform for modeling neurodevelopmental disorders

mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.institution: University of California, Berkeley (or relevant lab)
mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.headline: UCL researchers reconstruct 10‑second movies from mouse visual‑cortex activity
mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.summary: Scientists at University College London used calcium imaging of neurons to recreate 10‑second video clips solely from mouse brain signals, revealing how visual input is internally represented.
highlights: Reconstructed videos matched unseen movies using a dynamic neural encoding model
Accuracy improved with data from more individual neurons in the visual cortex
Pixel correlation showed only small timing differences between original and reconstructed clips

240myr_fossil_dinosaur_timeline.headline: Tanzanian Fossil Redefines Timeline of Earliest Dinosaurs
240myr_fossil_dinosaur_timeline.summary: A 240‑million‑year‑old Tanzanian dicynodont named Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda forces scientists to revise the earliest dinosaur timeline by showing the rocks are younger than previously thought.
highlights: Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda is the first record of the genus outside South America
The specimen, collected in 1963, lay in the Natural History Museum London for over 60 years before identification
Radiometric dating suggests Tanzanian rock layers are up to 10 million years younger than comparable South African deposits
The study was published in the peer‑reviewed Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology on September 15, 2026

chariklo_ring_dynamics.headline: Chariklo’s Rings Show Rapid Opacity Shifts, New JWST Data Reveal
chariklo_ring_dynamics.summary: Observations by the James Webb Space Telescope in 2022 indicate that Chariklo’s inner and outer rings altered their opacity within just a few years.
highlights: Inner ring became significantly more opaque while the outer ring grew clearer
Study led by the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia used stellar occultations to track changes
Findings published in Science Advances challenge assumptions about ring stability on small bodies

prime_assembly_universal_gene_therapies.headline: Prime Assembly Enables Multi‑Mutation Gene Repair, Paving Way for Universal Therapies
prime_assembly_universal_gene_therapies.summary: A new Nature paper shows prime assembly can stitch long DNA fragments into precise genome sites, correcting many mutations with a single approach.
